---
title: "Graph Traversal Practice"
subtitle: "Undirected Graph Traversal"
---

We have seen how we can traverse a graph using both DFS and BFS. Now let's apply this to a graph that does not look like the nodes and edges we have seen so far, but follows the same rules: A 2d grid.

:::{.panel}

Q - What are the neighbours of a cell in a grid?

A - The neighbours of a cell in a grid are the cells that are adjacent to it.

:::

### Exercise: Maze traversal

You are given a maze. The maze is a 2d grid of 0 and 1. Man-Pac starts at the top left (**S**) and wants to reach the bottom right (**T**). The 1s are coins he can collect as he moves through the grid; the 0s are walls.

::: {.static-graph-inline}
<div id="manpac-maze-preview"></div>
:::

In this case we do not have an adjacency list or matrix — the input itself is the grid. Before we can traverse, we need a way to ask: *from this cell, which cells can Man-Pac step onto?*

#### 1. Find valid neighbours

Assemble the steps below so `get_neighbours` returns every adjacent coin cell (a 1 that is up, down, left, or right — not a wall, and inside the grid). Once your plan looks right, click any coin cell on the maze to try it — the returned neighbours light up green, and are also listed underneath.

::: {.panel-grid}
::: {.panel}
<div id="manpac-neighbours-blocks"></div>
:::
::: {.panel}
<div id="manpac-neighbours-viz" class="cb-viz-placeholder"></div>
:::
:::

Now we are ready to start the traversals. In this case we also need to keep track of the **distance from start**. How do we do that?

:::{.callout-note}
We can track the distance whenever we are recording the visited nodes. When we move from the current cell to a neighbour, we add 1 to the distance.
:::

`get_neighbours` is now available. Using the same loop as before — pick from the bag, record each neighbour's distance in `tracking`, and stop as soon as the current cell **or one of its neighbours** is the target. `path_distance = tracking[target]` is the length of the path you found.

#### 2. BFS — queue

Explore layer by layer: pick the **first** cell in the bag (`pop(0)`). Press **Play** to watch the search, or **Step** to advance one line. The current cell is orange, newly tracked neighbours are green, and already-tracked cells are blue — with their distance from the start written on the cell.

::: {.panel-grid}
::: {.panel}
<div id="manpac-bfs-blocks"></div>
:::
::: {.panel}
<div id="manpac-bfs-viz" class="cb-viz-placeholder"></div>
:::
:::

#### 3. DFS — stack

Explore as deep as possible first: pick the **last** cell in the bag (`pop()`). Same blocks, different end of the bag.

::: {.panel-grid}
::: {.panel}
<div id="manpac-dfs-blocks"></div>
:::
::: {.panel}
<div id="manpac-dfs-viz" class="cb-viz-placeholder"></div>
:::
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import { mountCodeBlocksView } from "./js/code-blocks-view.js";
import {
  MANPAC_MAZE,
  MANPAC_START,
  MANPAC_TARGET,
  MANPAC_NEIGHBOURS_CODE_BLOCKS,
  MANPAC_NEIGHBOURS_CODE_OPTIONS,
  MANPAC_BFS_CODE_BLOCKS,
  MANPAC_BFS_CODE_OPTIONS,
  MANPAC_DFS_CODE_BLOCKS,
  MANPAC_DFS_CODE_OPTIONS,
  mountNotebookMazeGrid,
  mountManpacNeighboursView,
  mountManpacTraversalView,
} from "./js/maze-helpers.js";
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
manpacPreview = mountNotebookMazeGrid(
  document.querySelector("#manpac-maze-preview"),
  MANPAC_MAZE,
  {
    start: MANPAC_START,
    target: MANPAC_TARGET,
    cellSize: 28,
    caption: "S = start (top left), T = target (bottom right). 1 = coin / open, 0 = wall.",
  }
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
manpacNeighboursBlocks = mountCodeBlocksView(
  document.querySelector("#manpac-neighbours-blocks"),
  MANPAC_NEIGHBOURS_CODE_BLOCKS,
  MANPAC_NEIGHBOURS_CODE_OPTIONS
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
manpacNeighboursViz = mountManpacNeighboursView(
  document.querySelector("#manpac-neighbours-viz"),
  MANPAC_MAZE,
  {
    start: MANPAC_START,
    target: MANPAC_TARGET,
    cellSize: 30,
    getPython: () => manpacNeighboursBlocks.toPython(),
  }
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
manpacBfsBlocks = mountCodeBlocksView(
  document.querySelector("#manpac-bfs-blocks"),
  MANPAC_BFS_CODE_BLOCKS,
  MANPAC_BFS_CODE_OPTIONS
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
manpacBfsViz = mountManpacTraversalView(
  document.querySelector("#manpac-bfs-viz"),
  MANPAC_MAZE,
  {
    start: MANPAC_START,
    target: MANPAC_TARGET,
    heading: "BFS traversal",
    bagFooter: "ordered list — pop from the left (queue)",
    cellSize: 28,
    stepDelayMs: 400,
    getPython: () => manpacBfsBlocks.toPython(),
    onStep: (frame) => {
      if (frame?.blockId) manpacBfsBlocks.highlight(frame.blockId);
      else manpacBfsBlocks.clearHighlight();
    },
  }
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
manpacDfsBlocks = mountCodeBlocksView(
  document.querySelector("#manpac-dfs-blocks"),
  MANPAC_DFS_CODE_BLOCKS,
  MANPAC_DFS_CODE_OPTIONS
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
manpacDfsViz = mountManpacTraversalView(
  document.querySelector("#manpac-dfs-viz"),
  MANPAC_MAZE,
  {
    start: MANPAC_START,
    target: MANPAC_TARGET,
    heading: "DFS traversal",
    bagFooter: "ordered list — pop from the right (stack)",
    cellSize: 28,
    stepDelayMs: 400,
    getPython: () => manpacDfsBlocks.toPython(),
    onStep: (frame) => {
      if (frame?.blockId) manpacDfsBlocks.highlight(frame.blockId);
      else manpacDfsBlocks.clearHighlight();
    },
  }
)
```


### Exercise: Flood Fill

You are given a 2d image. Implement the "bucket-fill" where you can select a single cell and fill the entire area connected to it with the same color.

The image is a 2D list of hex colour strings (`pixel_array`). A section of the pixel array is shown here:

<5 x 10 grid with hex values written in each cell>

Click a pixel on the right to choose the start cell, pick a fill colour, then implement `floodFill(pixel_array, start, color)`. Modify the grid **in place** — neighbours are the four adjacent cells. Press **Play** to watch the image update as your code paints it.

Hint: This time the "neighbours" are adjacent cells that have the **same** colour. This time you are free to either use a separate function to find the neighbours, or do it inline.

::: {.panel-grid}
::: {.panel}
<div id="flood-fill-editor"></div>
:::
::: {.panel}
<div id="flood-fill-viz" class="cb-viz-placeholder"></div>
:::
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import { PythonEditorInput } from "./js/python-editor-input.js";
import {
  PIXEL_ARRAY,
  floodFillStarterCode,
  mountFloodFillViz,
} from "./js/flood-fill.js";
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
floodEditor = PythonEditorInput.mountPlayable(
  document.querySelector("#flood-fill-editor"),
  {
    heading: "Python",
    defaultCode: floodFillStarterCode(),
  }
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
floodViz = mountFloodFillViz(document.querySelector("#flood-fill-viz"), {
  editor: floodEditor,
  pixelArray: PIXEL_ARRAY,
})
```
